standard.title: Methods of Physical Tests for Hydraulic Cement — Part 2: Determination of Fineness by Blaine Air Permeability Method (Second Revision)
standard.description: This Indian Standard (Part 2) covers the laboratory testing procedure for determining the fineness of hydraulic cement using the Blaine air permeability apparatus, measuring the specific surface area of cement particles per unit mass.
standard.scope: This Indian Standard (Part 2) covers the laboratory testing procedure for determining the fineness of hydraulic cement using the Blaine air permeability apparatus, measuring the specific surface area of cement particles per unit mass.

certification.description: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 4031 (Part 2) is an analytical testing standard rather than a direct consumer product, it does not carry an individual physical 'ISI Mark' product stamp on its own. However, compliance with its testing and calibration protocols is legally mandatory for NABL laboratory accreditation audits (under ISO/IEC 17025) and for declaring compliance of finished cement bags carrying the physical ISI Mark under product codes like IS 269.
requirements: Under the active Amendment No. 2 (March 2017), National Council for Cement and Building Materials certified reference material NCB CRM-1001A must be used as the mandatory reference cement to calibrate and determine the apparatus constant.

Specifies that the mandatory calibration reference cement, NCB CRM-1001A, is officially obtained from the Centre for Quality Management, Standards & Calibration Services, National Council for Cement and Building Materials located at Ballabgarh (Haryana).
Fineness is measured by observing the time taken for a fixed quantity of air to flow through a compacted cement bed of specified density, porosity, and volume.

Under standard testing conditions, the specific surface area (S) of cement is directly proportional to the square root of the air flow time (√t), calculated as: S = K * √t, where K represents the calibrated apparatus constant.
The resulting fineness value must be expressed as specific surface in square centimeters per gram (cm²/g) or square meters per kilogram (m²/kg).

Final observed or calculated test and analytical values must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.
